questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the role of each of the following types of system buses:

(i) Address bus. (2 marks)

(ii) Control bus. (2 marks)

(iii) Data bus. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Address bus (2 marks).** The address bus carries the *address* of the memory location (or of the input/output device) that the processor wants to read from or write to. It is one-way: the addresses travel from the processor to memory and to the devices. The number of lines of the address bus fixes the amount of memory that can be addressed: $n$ lines can address $2^n$ locations.

**(ii) Control bus (2 marks).** The control bus carries the control and timing signals that coordinate all the parts of the computer, for example memory read, memory write, clock, interrupt request and bus request signals. It is sent mainly by the control unit and tells the components *what to do and when* (read or write, which device is selected).

**(iii) Data bus (2 marks).** The data bus carries the actual *data and instructions* between the processor, the main memory and the input/output devices. It is two-way (bidirectional). Its width (8, 16, 32 or 64 lines) fixes how many bits can be moved at one time.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly describe the characteristics of a compact disc (CD) in terms of:

(i) How data is stored. (3 marks)

(ii) The physical layout of tracks and sectors on the CD. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) How data is stored (3 marks).**

- A CD is a flat plastic disc with a thin reflective (metal) layer protected by a transparent coating.
- Data is recorded as a pattern of tiny **pits** (hollows burned or pressed into the reflective layer) and **lands** (the flat areas between pits).
- The data is read *optically*: a low-power laser beam is shone on the spinning disc and the amount of light reflected back is detected by a sensor. A land reflects the light strongly while a pit scatters it, so the sensor sees changes that are decoded as the binary digits 1 and 0.
- A CD is a read-only medium (CD-ROM) or, in the case of CD-R and CD-RW, a medium that can be written once or many times by a stronger laser.

**(ii) Physical layout of tracks and sectors (2 marks).**

- Unlike a magnetic hard disk, which has many separate concentric circles, a CD has **one continuous spiral track** that starts near the centre of the disc and winds outwards to the edge.
- The spiral track is divided into **sectors** of the same physical length. Because the sectors have equal length, the outer turns of the spiral hold more sectors than the inner turns, and the disc spins faster near the centre and slower near the edge so that the data passes the laser at a constant speed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Sketch and label a block diagram of a simplified computer system, that shows the stages of information processing. (3 marks)

(ii) Describe the main activity of each stage and give one example of a device used. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Block diagram (3 marks).** The stages of information processing are input, processing, output, with storage linked to the processing stage:

```text
  +---------+      +--------------------+      +----------+
  |  INPUT  | ---> |     PROCESSING     | ---> |  OUTPUT  |
  | (data)  |      | (CPU + main memory)|      |(information)
  +---------+      +---------+----------+      +----------+
                             ^
                             |  save / retrieve
                             v
                       +-----------+
                       |  STORAGE  |
                       +-----------+
```

**(ii) Main activity of each stage and an example of a device (6 marks).**

| Stage | Main activity | Example of a device |
|---|---|---|
| Input | Data and instructions are entered or captured and converted into a form the computer can process (binary). | Keyboard (also mouse, scanner, microphone) |
| Processing | The central processing unit carries out the instructions: it performs the arithmetic and logical operations on the data held in main memory and controls the other parts. | CPU (microprocessor) |
| Output | The results of processing are presented to the user in a form that people can understand (text, pictures, sound). | Monitor (also printer, loudspeaker) |
| Storage | Data, programs and results are kept so that they can be used again later, even when the power is off. | Hard disk (also flash disk, CD) |
